shots.caption: You say the work once, in your own currency.
Sage compiles it into milestones, each with a verification contract.
J$10,000 in two parts — stamped at today's rate, funded into a vault with hard caps.
From here it spends without me. It can never spend outside the vault's limits.

shots.card:
The agent proposes.
The vault disposes.

shots.caption: Public work asks everyone to prove they are one person, once. No name, no document, no country.
Fifty slots need fifty people. The operator who took ten of ten slots with twelve wallets would have needed ten humans.
Recipients don't need a bank or a wallet app. Chat is the account.
Sage pays on Starknet into an escrow only the recipient can open — and publishes a receipt that proves the money moved without saying to whom.
And it refuses. This is a farm: one operator, twelve wallets, drawn from the chain.
Forty percent of judged work is refused, with the reason on the record. A rail that pays everything is a leak.
Every verified payout accrues to a work record with deterministic credit signals — formulas over receipts, never a score.
And Sage lends against it: an advance sized by the lender's multiple on verified inflow.
Repaid by the next verified payouts through a waterfall. Capital out, capital back in, from the ledger the agent wrote.
Fund it once and stop deciding.
Sage chooses what work to buy next — where, never how much — and proposes it with its reason before a dollar leaves. You can veto any move.
Fees: a flat ten cents a settlement; recipients keep every cent. Settlement: minutes, verification included.
Credit without collateral: an advance against verified inflow. Regional flow: obligations priced in the region's own currencies.
